grade.basis: Independent notation-based advisory grade. Representative notation inspected across all four movements, not merely the opening: Andante quarter=70 uses exposed upper first-viola cantilena, small rapid ornaments and chromatic counterpoint above moving/pizzicato lower parts (PDF2,4); Allegro quarter=130 has repeated off-beat entries, scalar/ornamental sixteenths, shifting alto/treble reading and sustained independent rhythmic layers (PDF7,9,13,15); Lento quarter=55 retains exposed melodic ornament and contrapuntal tuning rather than just easy block chords (PDF18); Vivo quarter=130 has extended lower-part sixteenths, first-viola chromatic and scalar runs, changing bow articulation, ricochet-marked triplet figures and upper-register climaxes (PDF22,24,26). Viola 1 is the principal technical ceiling, although viola 4 has considerable motor stamina and inner parts are real chamber partners. This cumulative demand supports pre-diploma/ABRSM ARSM–RCM10 equivalent rather than an intermediate quartet; short flourish notation alone does not justify diploma level. As calibration, Mozart K423/424 duos at 6 provide a broadly comparable advanced independent-string player band, while Prokofiev Op56 at 8 represents substantially greater sustained professional complexity. Tonal idiom and a generally shared pulse make the coordination practical within the player band: no automatic ensemble uplift. Whole-work primary context and substantial multi-movement notation support medium confidence with approximately one-level uncertainty; not exhaustive certification.
